prompt: Create one distinct original character portrait of Prior Aymer as first seen travelling in Walter Scott's Ivanhoe, chapter II paragraphs 4–5 and 12–13. A handsome, somewhat corpulent medieval churchman with an affable worldly expression and a small knowing twinkle in his eyes, humane and individually recognisable rather than an evil monk caricature. He wears a finely woven ivory monastic mantle and hood made from rich Flanders cloth, grey-brown fur lining turned back at the sleeve edges, and a handsome GOLD CLASP securing the mantle at his throat. The hood can rest over the back of his head and shoulders; avoid displaying an invented hairstyle. He is seated comfortably and skilfully on a well-fed ambling MULE: show enough of its gentle head, long ears and decorated bridle with small SILVER BELLS at the lower side of this three-quarter portrait to distinguish it from a horse. His hands hold the reins naturally; no staff of office or weapon. Quiet English woodland road, soft green dusk and oak foliage, no other people. Fine painterly oil and watercolour literary book-plate style, restrained cream, old gold, brown fur and woodland greens, natural skin and expressive eyes, clearly legible at small portrait-card scale. This is his first travelling outfit, NOT the scarlet cap, jewelled banquet cope or fantastically pointed boots of later descriptions. No bishop's mitre, crown, modern clerical collar, rosary added as a principal prop, oversized cross, actor likeness, sinister supernatural lighting, future captivity or ransom scene, text, logo or watermark. Single human portrait with his mule as the source-grounded mount.
originalReview: Opened original: affable somewhat corpulent churchman, fine ivory cloth, gold throat clasp, turned fur sleeve edges and hood; rides a visibly long-eared mule with decorated bridle and silver bells. Face is distinct and humane; no later banquet cap, pointed boots, captivity or ransom. Hands and reins are coherent. Approved candidate.
